solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: If clue initially reads badly, strike it!

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, in a scrambled order
only the opening letter of reads is used

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver says that if a clue reads poorly, it should be struck out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives R from reads, and 'badly' rearranges IF CLUE R.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucifer is an old word for a friction match, the thing you strike.

clue.text: Bet core part of livelihood's to be superseded by ChatGPT, etc

indicators.note: everything inside the outer letters of livelihood is the part to be swapped
the core is pushed out and replaced by the next piece

parts.note: the word livelihood itself, with its possessive s read as is
ChatGPT and its like are AI, artificial intelligence

explanation.surface: A worker wagers that their means of income will be replaced by chatbots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core part of' marks IVELIHOO, all but the L and D of livelihood, and 'to be superseded by' replaces it with AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, as in laying a wager, so it can mean wagered.

clue.text: Accountant cycling in retirement, huffs and puffs and rests

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: cycling sends a letter round from the front of the word to the back
in retirement means going back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: to huff and puff is to pant, breathing heavily

explanation.surface: A retired accountant out cycling, wheezing and stopping for breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses PANTS to STNAP and 'cycling' moves its S from the front to the back, giving TNAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief daytime dozes are short periods of sleep.

clue.text: It's strange if one daughter's not had drink after sacrifice in God's name

parts.note: to forgo is to give up

parts.words: It's strange if one daughter's not
parts.note: ODDNESS (the fact of being strange) with one D for daughter removed
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it odd that one daughter has not had a drink after the religious offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It’s strange' stands for ODDNESS, and losing one of its two Ds leaves one. The order is FORGO first, then the rest, which 'had' the drink after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalent exclamations of exasperation, one invoking goodness and the other God.

clue.text: It can be difficult to find equal treatment with power ceded to queen

definitions.text: It can be difficult to find

indicators.note: with introduces the circumstance under which the swap of letters happens
the power letter is given up in favour of the queen letter

parts.note: parity is equality of status or treatment
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
R is the abbreviation for regina, queen

explanation.surface: Fairness is hard to come by when a monarch takes control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ceded to' replaces the P of PARITY with R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something uncommon, hence hard to come across.

clue.text: Hydrogen injected into carbon, mainly to support frame

indicators.note: injected into places hydrogen right after carbon

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to assist is to support

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab where hydrogen is added to carbon to strengthen a framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base framework of a vehicle.

clue.text: Peach or prune that is seen peeled

parts.note: to prune is to cut
i.e. = that is
SPIED (seen) with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Two fruits, a peach and a prune, with something noticed about one being peeled.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit-bowl surface puts 'Peach' and 'prune' side by side, but here 'Peach' is a person and 'prune' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal terms of endearment: calling someone a peach means they are lovely, as does the answer.

clue.text: Bit of a hoo-ha derailed precautions at llama farm ultimately

indicators.note: a derailed train leaves its tracks in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: 'ultimately' means in the end, so the last letters of llama and farm are taken

parts.note: the last letters of llamA and farM

explanation.surface: A fuss at a llama farm when safety measures went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the fuss real; the answer says the fuss was over nothing much.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a great commotion over a trivial matter, which is what a hoo-ha usually amounts to.

clue.text: Dreadful opening piece from Italian serial composer

indicators.note: the letters are put in a dreadful mess, scrambled into a new order
only the first letter of Italian is taken

explanation.surface: A dire opening episode of an Italian television serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening piece from' gives I, and 'Dreadful' rearranges I and SERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Salieri was an Italian composer at the Viennese court, famed as Mozart's supposed rival.

clue.text: Wear this running in street?

indicators.note: 'in' puts the jumble inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: WEAR THIS jumbled

indicators.note: letters left running about are out of order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: ST = street, the abbreviation, which goes round the jumble

explanation.surface: Advice on what to put on for a jog along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: read straight, it recommends the answer as running gear.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: read straight, the clue describes a loose cotton top, the kind of thing worn for a run down the road.

clue.text: Try to make sense of painter prettifying houses

indicators.note: to house is to hold inside, so the words before it contain the answer

parts.note: the letters run across the gap, after pa- and before -tifying

explanation.surface: An artist making houses look prettier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like the painter's subject; it is the instruction that the two words contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to construe or explain the meaning of something.

clue.text: Bit of Scrabble on Boxing Day, Mark?

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it

parts.note: a Scrabble tile
D = day

explanation.surface: Someone asks Mark whether he played Scrabble on Boxing Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing Day' reads as the holiday after Christmas, but 'Boxing' is the container and 'Day' is just D. 'Mark' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypernym: a squiggle written over a letter, as in Spanish ñ, is one kind of diacritical mark.

clue.text: Feeding spirit, shattered tenor had kip, missing intro to national anthem

indicators.note: feeding says the jumbled letters are put into the spirit word, as food into a mouth

parts.note: zest means spirit or energy

indicators.note: shattered says the letters are broken and reassembled
missing says a letter is taken out of tenor
intro to picks the first letter of national

explanation.surface: An exhausted tenor napped, skipping the opening of the national anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: TENOR without N, plus HAD and KIP, rearranges to ADOKTHEPRI, which goes into ZEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's coronation anthem is sung at every British coronation since 1727.

clue.text: Wet blankets outside during short run

indicators.note: 'outside' puts the first word around the second

parts.note: a misery is a gloomy killjoy
in = during

explanation.surface: Damp bedding is left out while a brief spell passes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'wet blanket' and a 'misery' are both people who spoil the fun. 'Short run' is television, not athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: Television sense of run: a drama shown over a small number of episodes has only a brief run.

clue.text: What's here: villains ideally?

indicators.note: 'what's here' asks what is contained in the words that follow, so the answer is held within them

parts.note: the letters run across the gap, after vill- and before -ally

explanation.surface: A caption pointing at the place where criminals ought to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes itself: it sits in the middle of 'villains ideally', and ideally villains are in prison, which is the slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: slang for serving a prison sentence, where villains ideally are, and also where the answer sits in the phrase.

clue.text: Sign me up to gain access to beauty contract

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person
'I'm in!' is what you say to join something

explanation.surface: A would-be model asks to be signed so she can get a beauty contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun going with 'beauty', but it is the verb: shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, verb sense: to become smaller or shrink.

clue.text: Continue unchanging message, penning discrimination and slurs

parts.note: to be is to remain as you are, as in 'let it be'

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so the message encloses the next piece

parts.note: an SMS is a text message
an ear for music is discrimination between sounds

explanation.surface: A repeated message containing prejudice, and abusive remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discrimination' sounds like prejudice, which suits 'slurs', but here it is a fine ear for sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym, verb sense: to smear or sully someone's reputation.

clue.text: I note response to where duke's suffering embarrassment

parts.note: I as written
N = note
'Where?' 'There!'
D = duke

explanation.surface: Someone writes that the duke is embarrassed about where he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embarrassment' here is the old sense of financial difficulty, as in pecuniary embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from red ink in accounts: being overdrawn, which is the dated money sense of embarrassment.

clue.text: Lacy kit's modelled in such a way?

definitions.text: Lacy kit's modelled in such a way?

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are shaped into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A catwalk critic suggests the lace outfit was worn in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the adverb describes how lacy kit might well be modelled.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: read straight, the clue asks for a manner of modelling lingerie, and cheap, tasteless is the manner meant.

clue.text: Starting to gag's consistent with smoke

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Gag
as per = in keeping with, consistent with

explanation.surface: Choking is what you'd expect from breathing smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The gagging surface fits: a cheap cigarette makes you gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: an old word for a cheap cigarette, and a cigarette is a smoke.

clue.text: Vivid description of old Northerner having curries regularly

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of curries is taken

parts.note: the even letters of cUrRiEs

explanation.surface: An account of an old man from the north who is always eating curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northerner' suggests someone from northern England; the Picts were early inhabitants of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: an account so vivid it creates an image, as when a writer paints one in words.

clue.text: Ray's maybe aloof

indicators.note: 'maybe' flags that a ray is only one example of the class meant

parts.note: the possessive 's means 'of'
a ray is a fish

explanation.surface: A remark that someone called Ray might be standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' reads as a man's name; he is a flatfish, and the possessive turns him into 'of fish', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: short for standoffish, cool and distant in manner.

clue.text: Sorry if this is crude way to make showman be shown?

definitions.meaning: said as an apology for swearing

definitions.text: way to make showman be shown?
definitions.meaning: 'my' in French is MA; excuse (let off) MA from SHOWMAN and you get SHOWN

explanation.surface: An apology for bad language, plus an odd riddle about a showman.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the trick: read the phrase literally, as 'leave out MA', and SHOWMAN becomes SHOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom plus a literal reading: the stock apology for swearing, and an instruction to drop the French word for my.

clue.text: One piece of information is all I have uncovered

indicators.note: the outer letters are removed, leaving the inside exposed

parts.note: an estate is all a person owns

explanation.surface: Someone admits that a single fact is the only thing they have revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the outer E's from ESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat, short for statistic, is a single item of numerical data.

clue.text: Casual trade in island, American island

indicators.note: 'in' places the first piece inside the letter that follows

parts.note: I = island
A = American
biz is informal for business, as in showbiz

explanation.surface: A description of informal commerce on an island owned by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'island' is the definition; the first is only I.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, off Spain.

clue.text: Aptly-placed lawyer's battleground

parts.note: AG = Attorney General
a lawyer is aptly placed in court

explanation.surface: A lawyer is in the right spot for a courtroom battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ask where a lawyer is aptly placed and the answer is the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the field in northern France where Henry V won his 1415 battle.

clue.text: Short head's feature of mouse?

parts.note: shy of = short of, as in two votes shy
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A horse beaten by a short head, or a note on a mouse's small head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short head' sounds like a racing margin. The question mark flags the mouse: a mousy person is timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense of mouse: a timid, retiring person, whose defining trait is bashfulness.

clue.text: Maximally in pain after irrational hour boomeranging

indicators.note: a boomerang comes back, so the letters are read backwards
'after' sends 'pain' behind the reversed piece in the answer

parts.note: pi is an irrational number
H = hour
a pain is a pest, a nuisance

explanation.surface: At an absurd hour of pain returning, someone is at their very limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the fashion sense, and 'maximally' makes it a superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang superlative: most fashionable, where 'in' means in vogue.
